# MM-P2-L4-RR01 Maintenance manual - Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-RR01

Scope
This document defines preventive maintenance and corrective restart procedures for the Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) installed on line P2-L4. It covers mechanical inspection, lubrication, mandrel clamp verification, bearing condition checks, and records to be kept after each activity. For related operational and safety procedures, see SOP-P2-L4-02, SOP-P2-L4-03, and SOP-P2-L4-04.

Background and rationale
Radial ring rolling mills are subject to high radial and axial loads during operation. Wear accumulates on bearings and on the mandrel clamp system. Proper clamp bolt preload and timely lubrication reduce vibration, prevent ovality of formed parts, and extend component life. The listed mandrel clamp bolt torque and lubrication interval are derived from factory fitment data and field trial run-in behavior for this specific machine arrangement. Adhering to the specified torque minimizes clamp slippage without overstressing fasteners. The specified lubrication interval balances operating duty cycles with grease life to prevent metal-to-metal contact in the main roll bearings.

Tools
- Calibrated torque wrench capable of applying the required torque
- Socket set compatible with mandrel clamp bolt heads
- Bearing grease gun with fittings compatible with main roll bearing grease points
- Clean lint-free rags and approved solvent for wipe-down (per SOP-P2-L4-03)
- Dial indicator and magnetic base for runout checks
- Vibration analyzer and handheld strobe for dynamic inspection (optional for trend analysis)
- Maintenance log forms and mill usage runtime report (see Records to Keep)
- Personal protective equipment as specified in SOP-P2-L4-02 and SOP-P2-L4-04

Procedure
General safety: Verify lockout/tagout in accordance with SOP-P2-L4-02 before performing any maintenance. Ensure electrical and hydraulic energy sources are isolated and stored energy is bled. Wear PPE required by SOP-P2-L4-04.

Mandrel clamp bolt torque verification and adjustment
- Remove any protective covers to access the mandrel clamp bolts. Clean the bolt heads and threads of debris and old lubricant following methods in SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, set the wrench to 525 N·m. Slowly apply torque to each mandrel clamp bolt until the wrench indicates the specified value. Apply torque in an alternating pattern around the mandrel to attain even clamp loading; the alternating approach prevents eccentric clamp loading and ensures uniform mandrel contact.
- After initial tightening, rotate the mandrel slowly by hand and check clamp engagement. If there is evidence of clamp slippage or rotation relative to the mandrel, repeat the torque application sequence.
- Rationale: Specifying a consistent torque reduces variability between maintenance crews and prevents under- or over-clamping which can lead to product defects or bolt fatigue.

Main roll bearing lubrication
- Confirm machine is at rest and bearings are at ambient conditions. Wipe grease fittings clean before attaching the grease gun to prevent contamination.
- Apply grease using the bearing grease gun until fresh grease is observed at the seal or purge point, taking care not to introduce contaminants. Record the lubrication event in the maintenance log with machine runtime at the time of service.
- The main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 195 hours. Schedule the next lubrication based on accumulated runtime and verify during shift handover.
- Rationale: Lubrication at the prescribed interval ensures a protective film is maintained on bearing surfaces. Over-greasing can be as damaging as under-greasing; follow the purge indicator or manufacturer guidance during application.

Bearing and roll condition inspection
- Perform a visual inspection for leaks, seal integrity, and abnormal wear on roll journals and housings. Use a dial indicator to measure runout; document readings and compare to prior records for trend detection.
- Perform a vibration scan during a light run if conditions allow (follow SOP-P2-L4-02 for restart checks). Compare spectrum signatures to baseline trends to identify bearing degradation early.
- Rationale: Trend monitoring allows maintenance to be scheduled proactively and avoids unplanned shutdowns.

Examples and special cases
- Example: If after applying the specified mandrel clamp bolt torque a clamp bolt shows evidence of thread stripping or cannot hold torque, remove and tag the hardware for replacement per spare parts procedure. Log the event and notify engineering to review clamp alignment before reassembly.
- Example: If excessive grease purge occurs or bearings feel unusually warm after lubrication, stop further lubrication and escalate to maintenance engineering for contamination analysis.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry for each torque verification including date, technician initials, torque wrench serial or calibration ID, and confirmation that 525 N·m was applied.
- Lubrication record noting the date, technician initials, grease type, and machine runtime at the time of service. Include note that the main roll bearing lubrication interval for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L4-RR01) is 195 hours and the calculated next due runtime.
- Inspection checklist documenting visual findings, runout measurements, vibration scan results, and any corrective actions taken.
- Nonconformance report for any failed hardware or abnormal findings, cross-referenced to work order number and corrective action plan.

Acceptance criteria
- All mandrel clamp bolts must register 525 N·m when checked with a calibrated torque wrench. No bolt shall show signs of thread damage or plastic deformation after torque application.
- Main roll bearings must be lubricated within the prescribed lubrication interval and show no signs of contamination or severe leakage on inspection. Acceptance is based on clean purge appearance and normal running temperature and vibration profiles relative to baseline.
- Runout and vibration measurements must fall within historical trending limits as documented in the machine condition log. Any deviation beyond established trend thresholds requires corrective action before returning to production.
- Records for torque application, lubrication, inspections, and any corrective actions must be complete and filed in the document control system following SOP-P2-L4-03.

References
SOP-P2-L4-02  
SOP-P2-L4-03  
SOP-P2-L4-04

Revision history and approvals are maintained in the document control system.
